answer: Persistent Attention Ledger. Each agent identity accrues standing only through verified, spaced interactions with distinct peers; a new identity enters at a low-trust grove and climbs ranks slowly. To sustain N identities, an attacker must supply N agents continuously answering liveness challenges and maintaining distinct behavioral profiles, like keeping many falcons aloft at once. Idle identities decay off the ridge within days, so the attacker pays ongoing compute and orchestration cost per identity, not a one-time fee.
